sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Java build tool interview questions cover Maven and Gradle in interview depth — Maven lifecycle phases, dependency scopes and conflict resolution, multi-module projects, profiles, publishing artifacts; Gradle build scripts, the dependency DSL, the wrapper, multi-module builds, incremental builds, and the Maven-vs-Gradle decision (and Bazel as the third option). Use this page for any role that touches CI builds, library publishing, or migrating between build tools.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Maven and Gradle solve the same problem differently:

- **Maven** — declarative XML, fixed lifecycle, batteries-included.
- **Gradle** — programmable Groovy/Kotlin DSL, incremental builds, configurable cache.
- **Bazel** — the third option for monorepos at scale.
- **Wrapper** (`mvnw` / `gradlew`) is non-negotiable — pin the build tool version.
- **Reproducible builds** — no `SNAPSHOT` in releases.

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Comparisons** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Gradle build** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Maven build** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.
- **Scenario-based** — applied questions tying multiple topics together. Drill these *last*, after the fundamentals are sharp.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **Maven scopes** — compile / provided / runtime / test; mention `provided` for servlet APIs.
- **Gradle config-cache** — modern speedup; opt-in via flag.
- **Multi-module builds** — `<modules>` in Maven, `include 'a','b'` in Gradle.
- **Dependency conflict** — Maven nearest-wins, Gradle highest-version-wins.
- **Publishing** — `mvn deploy` vs `gradle publish`; both need credentials in settings, not in code.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For a new Spring Boot project I'd reach for <Maven for simplicity | Gradle for build speed>, pin the version via wrapper, manage deps with BOMs, fail the build on convergence conflicts, and publish via CI with credentials from the secret store."*
